question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087655/plots/circle-7e1bc5767197aa888a5d5f49b1f3919b35e14679a6914a2de662015fd9ba136e.png)

What is the equation of the circle given above?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

From the picture, we see that our circle is centered at $C(5,6)$ and the radius of the circle is $r=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-5)^{2}+(y-6)^{2} & ={2}^{2} \\ (x-5)^{2}+(y-6)^{2} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087655/plots/circle-c5fd4b9d0318be86691224dc5ee28788a370dde237b6f8a3248eeec215afd9a8.png)

What is the equation of the circle given above?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

From the picture, we see that our circle is centered at $C(\frac{5}{4},- \frac{5}{4})$ and the radius of the circle is $r=\frac{11}{3}.$ Therefore, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-\frac{5}{4})^{2}+(y-(- \frac{5}{4}))^{2} & =(\frac{11}{3})^{2} \\ (x-\frac{5}{4})^{2}+(y+\frac{5}{4})^{2} & =\frac{121}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
